dedupe_keys.name: ireland european union resilience of critical entities regulations 2024 and national strategy 2026 2029

description: This Office of Emergency Planning page sets out how Ireland applies the EU Directive on the resilience of critical entities. In October 2024 the Minister for Defence signed the European Union (Resilience of Critical Entities) Regulations 2024, S.I. No. 559 of 2024, covering energy, transport, banking, financial market infrastructure, health, drinking water, wastewater, digital infrastructure, public administration, space and large-scale food production and distribution. The page lists the competent authority for each of the 11 sectors, among them the Commission for Regulation of Utilities, the Irish Aviation Authority, the Commission for Railway Regulation, the Central Bank, the Environmental Protection Agency and ComReg, and names the Office of Emergency Planning as the single point of contact. It links the National Strategy on the Resilience of Critical Entities 2026-2029, which sets governance, criteria for identifying critical entities, their obligations and resilience measures, and the three-yearly National Risk Assessment updated for the regulations. Format and access: web page with PDF files. Licence: gov.ie content, reuse terms not read; free. Caveats: the identified critical entities themselves are not published. It gives the sector and authority structure needed for resilience and hazard exposure studies of Irish infrastructure. Related catalogue records are the National Risk Assessment for Ireland 2023 and the EU CER Directive.
